newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Rabo says declining beer market report misquoted.
newsitem.headline: Rabo says declining beer market report misquoted.

text.p: Dutch cooperative Rabobank said on Friday newspaper reports saying the bank had forecast a five percent decline of the European beer market by the year 2000, were based on a misunderstanding.
"The expectation... is that beer consumption within Europe between now and the year 2000 will show a decline of around one percent," Rabo said in a statement.
Last October, Rabo's company magazine Rabovisie had mentioned the five percent decline, referring to a still to be published Rabo report on 'The World Beer Market'.
The report will be published at the end of this month or at the beginning of February, Rabo said, and did not forecast such a decline.
Shares in Dutch brewer Heineken NV closed 5.50 guilders lower on Friday at 293.50 guilders after hitting a low of 291.00 guilders at the opening, hurt by speculation over the report.
Grolsch lost 2.10 guilders to end at 66 guilders, up from its day low of 65.00 guilders.
